title: Environment Configuration Map
purpose: Show which 20+ environment variables feed which modules — 7 env var domains mapped to their config files, initialization points, and consuming runtime modules. Highlight the 3 .env file copies and the distinction between server-side and client-exposed vars.
audience: DevOps engineers, developers configuring local environment
description: Complete mapping of every environment variable used by the PoDM backend and frontend across 7 domains: Supabase (SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY), Stripe (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY), Cloudflare R2 (R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, R2_ACCOUNT_ID, R2_BUCKET_NAME, R2_PUBLIC_BUCKET_NAME, R2_PUBLIC_URL), Crypto (RPC_URL, CONTRACT_ADDRESS, CHAIN_ID), AI/OpenRouter (OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY), Email/SMTP (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS), and App Config (PORT, NODE_ENV, FRONTEND_URL, JWT_SECRET). Traces each variable from its source through its initialization file (supabaseClient.ts, stripeClient.ts, storage.service.ts, cryptoPayment.service.ts, ai.service.ts, email.service.ts) to the consuming services. Highlights the critical security issue: JWT_SECRET and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are exposed in the frontend .env file (client-accessible).

modules.label: supabaseClient.ts
modules.description: Initializes Supabase client with SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY for admin operations and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY for public operations.

modules.label: stripeClient.ts
modules.description: Initializes Stripe SDK with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY for backend payment operations.

modules.label: storage.service.ts
modules.description: Initializes R2 S3 client with R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, R2_ACCOUNT_ID, bucket names, and public URL.

modules.label: cryptoPayment.service.ts
modules.description: Initializes Ethers.js provider with RPC_URL, CONTRACT_ADDRESS, CHAIN_ID for on-chain verification.

modules.label: ai.service.ts
modules.description: Initializes OpenAI SDK with OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Routes to OpenRouter if key starts with sk-or-v1.

modules.label: email.service.ts
modules.description: Initializes Nodemailer transporter with SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS.

modules.label: index.ts / Server.ts
modules.description: Express server startup using PORT and NODE_ENV. CORS policy configured with FRONTEND_URL.

modules.label: auth.middleware.ts
modules.description: Uses JWT_SECRET for token signing/verification context (though actual verification is done via Supabase Auth API, not local decode).

entryPoints.label: .env file loaded at process start
entryPoints.description: All env vars loaded from .env file by dotenv at backend startup (index.ts) or injected by build system (Netlify, Render, Cloudflare).

exitPoints.label: Consuming Service
exitPoints.description: Each env var is consumed by its respective service at initialization time (import) or at runtime (lazy access).

preconditions: .env file exists in project root (backend) or podm-frontend/ (frontend)
All required env vars are defined—missing vars trigger runtime errors on first access
Frontend env vars must be prefixed with VITE_ to be exposed to client bundle
postconditions: Services are initialized with correct configuration on server start
Missing or invalid env vars cause initialization failure or runtime errors
Frontend bundle contains VITE_-prefixed vars in plaintext

errorPaths.trigger: Required env var missing at service initialization
errorPaths.destination: Service initialization fails—runtime error when service is first called
errorPaths.recovery: Add missing env var to .env and restart server

errorPaths.destination: Ethers.js provider fails to connect—crypto verification returns 503
errorPaths.recovery: Correct RPC_URL and restart. Transaction verification attempts retry with each request.

errorPaths.destination: ai.service.ts returns mock caption 'Enjoying the moment! ✨ #vibes (AI Key Missing)'
errorPaths.recovery: Add API key to environment and restart. Mock is a silent fallback with console.warn.

validationRules: Frontend env vars must be prefixed with VITE_ to be accessible in client code
Backend env vars should never be prefixed with VITE_ to avoid client exposure
JWT_SECRET and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must not be in frontend .env
businessRules: 3 copies of .env exist: backend root, podm-frontend/, and Netlify build-time vars
Only 4 VITE_-prefixed variables are exposed to the frontend bundle
securityConsiderations: CRITICAL: JWT_SECRET and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY committed in podm-frontend/.env—client-exposed
SMTP_PASS stored in plaintext environment variable—no encryption at rest
R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY provides full S3 API access to the bucket
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY provides full Stripe API access for payment operations
performanceConsiderations: All config clients are initialized once at import time—no lazy loading
Missing env vars cause hard failures on first service call (not on server start)

annotations.text: CRITICAL LEAK: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY exposed in podm-frontend/.env—any client can access
CRITICAL LEAK: JWT_SECRET exposed in podm-frontend/.env—clients could forge tokens if used for local decode
Missing key falls back to mock caption—graceful degradation but silent
